page: Microsoft Azure D16als_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dalv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.17 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2103.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24650.96 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12569.0. Memory performance exhibits a notable tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1216.64 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak at 36.85 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25%. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation show strong performance, while database operations, web serving, and software compilation fall into the average range.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and lack of local storage, the D16als_v6 offers a compute-focused hardware profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles and high single-core performance but do not demand large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, web serving, and lightweight containerized applications. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing due to the constrained memory capacity and weak large-block read memory bandwidth.
